newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - AKZO NOBEL PROFIT EDGES HIGHER IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - AKZO NOBEL PROFIT EDGES HIGHER IN 1996.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group Akzo Nobel NV on Thursday booked a record profit in 1996, up a modest amount from 1995 in an extremely difficult year, and saw higher net profits ahead.

"We stuck our necks out with our 1996 forecast but we have been able to achieve (that) projection despite slower than expected economic growth and a significant loss of operating revenue due to the pill controversy," chairman Cees van Lede told a results news conference.
Net profit rose to 1.318 billion guilders ($694.2 million) from 1.314 billion in 1995, on turnover of 22.44 billion guilders, up from 21.49 billion a year earlier.
The figures, at the lower end of analysts' forecasts of 1.30-1.35 billion guilders, were in line with Akzo's prediction of 1996 net profits roughly equal to 1995.
Akzo said it would pay a 1996 dividend of 7.50 guilders per share, up from 7.00 guilders in 1995.
Van Lede said this was a structural upgrade in pay-outs to reflect a reduction in the cyclical nature of Akzo, where cyclical businesses account for only 10 percent of turnover.
The group has been shifting into high-margin pharmaceuticals and coatings, reducing its chemicals and fibres exposure.
Fourth quarter net profit rose to 291 million guilders from 201 million in the same period of 1995, compared with forecasts of net profit from ordinary operations of 273-320 million.
Van Lede said quarterly results for the group tracked the economy, which picked up more slowly than initially anticipated.
"Fourth-quarter profits were better across the board, except that fibres remained under pressure," he said.
Based on expectations of continued moderate and stable growth in its most important markets, the company foresaw a higher net income over 1997.
Sales levels would remain roughly the same, despite the deconsolidation of activities generating around one billion guilders in turnover, he said.

Akzo sold its Salt America de-icing business to Cargill last August and will deconsolidate ROVIN, a polyvinyl chloride (PVC) alliance with Royal Dutch/Shell, and Delamine, its ethylene-amines joint venture with Japan's Tosoh.
Akzo said its pharmaceuticals and coatings businesses booked higher 1996 resuts, but chemicals and fibres were down.
Analysts were encouraged by the performance of the pharmaceuticals operation, where sales rose five percent to 3.95 billion guilders.
"The bottom-line figure was in line with our expectations, with pharma doing far better and chemicals somewhat disappointing," said Robert Jan Stassen of Bangert Pontier.
Prescription drugs unit Organon's results lagged 1995 due to lower results on contraceptive pills and costs of new product launches (fertility drug Puregon, anti-depressant Remeron).
Van Lede said restrictions in some countries on prescribing so-called third-generation low-dosage oral contraceptives had cost Organon some 70 million guilders in operating profit.
"We think the pill problems have bottomed out, although there are still some after-effects," he said.

The Organon decline was more than offset by higher profits by other business units, particularly Intervet (veterinary products) and Diosynth (specialised raw materials for the pharmaceuticals industry).
Coatings sales rose nine percent to 7.44 billion guilders, mainly due to currency effects and higher selling prices.
At the chemicals division sales rose five percent to 7.70 billion, reflecting positive currencies and higher volumes.
The fibre performance was dragged down by the very weak business climate but remained profitable.
"The figures were higher than I expected. The strong results from the pharma division were very encouraging -- very, very positive," said Quirijn Mulder, analyst at ING Barings.
But some analysts were sceptical about the outlook.

"The company has made a positive outlook but the only point is that they don't see sales growth. That should mean you're getting better results through cost savings and lower raw material prices, and that's not that impressive," said Peter Schouten of MeesPierson.
Akzo Nobel shares closed 4.10 guilders lower at 279.00 guilders in a mostly lower Amsterdam bourse.
